meta.title: FORGE — Striking S&C Template Library

Novice.conditioning_intensity: Zone 2 / conversational pace, technical round work at 50% output
Novice.notes: Priority is movement competency and connective-tissue tolerance before load. No max-effort work. Technical striking conditioning only — no live sparring pace intervals.

Beginner.conditioning_intensity: Zone 2-3, rounds at 60-70% output with technical focus
Beginner.notes: Introduce bilateral strength staples (squat/hinge/press/pull) and basic plyometrics. Conditioning starts to mimic round structure of the sport.

Intermediate.conditioning_intensity: Zone 3-4, race-pace rounds at 75-85% output, HIIT intervals introduced
Intermediate.notes: Strength-power bias. Contrast training (heavy lift + explosive movement) enters rotation. Conditioning volume matches actual bout/match round count.

Advanced.conditioning_intensity: Zone 4-5, fight-pace intervals at 85-95% output, sport-specific work capacity blocks
Advanced.notes: Individualized autoregulation (RPE/velocity-based). Camp-phase periodization required — GPP -> SPP -> Peak -> Taper. High neural cost work needs 48-72h separation from technical sparring.

Elite.intensity_main: 85-97% e1RM, VBT-monitored, RPE 8-10 only in peak block
Elite.conditioning_intensity: Fight-simulation pace, opponent-modeled round pacing, HRV/lactate-guided intensity
Elite.notes: S&C is fully subordinate to the fight calendar. Every block is built backward from fight night. Load management driven by daily readiness data, not the written plan — the plan is a default the coach is expected to override.

Muay Thai.rounds_note: 5x3 with 2-min rest is standard professional Thai pacing.

Kickboxing.rounds_note: 3x2 (K-1 rules) or 3x3 depending on ruleset — confirm sanctioning body.

Sanda.rounds_note: 3x2 with clinch/throw exchanges — conditioning must include repeated grip-and-off-balance efforts, not just striking output.

global_rules: Full commercial gym on-site — all barbell, dumbbell, kettlebell, cable/machine, and conditioning equipment listed above is available without restriction; no equipment constraint applies to any template in this library.
Technical/skill work (pad rounds, sparring, drilling) is programmed by the head coach separately — these templates cover S&C and conditioning only, built to not interfere with it.
Sequence within any session: neurologically demanding work first (power/plyo/Olympic-derivative) -> max strength -> conditioning/metabolic work last.
Heavy lower-body strength and high-volume plyometrics are never placed within 48h of a scheduled sparring session.
Deload every 4th week at 40-50% volume reduction, intensity maintained, for Intermediate level and above.
Fight-week (final 7 days before competition): all S&C stops except light neuromuscular activation (10-15min, sub-maximal) by day 3 out; full rest days 1-2 out.
Autoregulate: if a lifter misses velocity/RPE targets on the first work set by a wide margin, cut planned volume 20-30% that session rather than grinding through the written numbers.
Novice and Beginner levels do not perform max-effort (>90% e1RM) work under any circumstances.
All conditioning intensity/round-length numbers should be matched to the athlete's actual competition format (see sport_round_profiles) rather than used blindly.
